query: What learner needs and pain points appear in survey responses?

per_column.name: primary_need_category
per_column.rationale: The type/category of need expressed (e.g., pedagogical adaptation, digital tools, student engagement) is genuinely a constitutive aspect OF learner needs and pain points -- it decomposes WHAT the need is. However, it is a single multi-label taxonomy column rather than multiple orthogonal facets, so on its own it does not carve the concept into separable MECE aspects; the pipe-delimited overlapping values also blur any exclusivity.

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Bare positive/neutral/negative sentiment of the response is a generic affective measure, not a constitutive part of what a learner NEED or PAIN POINT is. Pain points are inherently negative-valenced; sentiment restates emotional tone rather than decomposing the concept into a component aspect.

per_column.name: engagement_impact
per_column.rationale: Engagement impact (high/medium/critical) measures a downstream consequence or severity dimension attached to the need, not a constitutive part of the need itself. It rates an effect rather than naming an aspect OF learner needs; 'critical' also mixes severity with the impact scale.

judge.rationale: Only one of the three added columns (primary_need_category) is a true meronymic facet of the concept, and even it is a single overlapping multi-label taxonomy rather than a set of orthogonal facets. Sentiment is a generic affective restatement and engagement_impact is an external severity/consequence predictor, neither of which is 'an aspect OF' learner needs and pain points. The set does not carve the concept into non-overlapping constitutive aspects, and it leaves major facets (e.g., need urgency/priority, affected stakeholder, resource vs. skill vs. support type, temporal/contextual dimension) uncovered. Both mutual exclusivity and exhaustiveness are weak.
